text:
maria: quick thought — i'd like to add a tiny 'runtime-shim' stage to model onboarding. it runs a focused set of checks (tokenization parity, kv-cache smoke, microbench for 1-2 seq lengths) against the target runtime binary before we mark a model as "onboarded". goal: surface runtime-only mismatches earlier and avoid canary rollback churn. what do folks think?

aj: +1 in principle. curious about scope — do you mean a new service that runs after our existing ingest bench, or a lightweight step inside the existing bench runner?

maria: lightweight step inside bench runner is my preference. keep it fast (30-90s) and deterministic. not a full microbench suite — just a few golden prompts + kv-cache probe and tokenization diff.

cheng: +1. watch out for tokenizers that are runtime-specific. we should version the tokenizer artifact with the model and pin it for the shim. otherwise we get false positives.

leo: can we make the shim pluggable? e.g. define an adapter interface with two ops: explainable_tokenize(input) -> tokens, and run_kv_probe(seq_len, prompt) -> trace. then runtime-specific adapters implement it. keeps code clean.

maria: exactly — adapter interface + small contract. sketch of the API I had in mind: 
```yaml
shim_contract: 
  - tokenize_check: 
      golden_inputs: ["hello world", "summarize: ..."]
      tolerance: 0
  - kv_cache_probe: 
      seq_lengths: [16, 256]
      expected_rtt_ms: 50
  - perf_micro: 
      tokens_per_sec_threshold: 5000
```

aj: nice. two tradeoffs: (1) where to run — hosted infra vs dedicated runner (cost/latency), (2) what to do on failure. Do we block onboarding, or mark model with advisory flag?

cheng: for (2) i'd err on blocking for tokenization mismatches and kv-cache crashes (they're high risk). perf threshold can be advisory (fail -> warn). Blocking onboarding has cost but prevents production surprises.

leo: for (1) we can run the shim in the same sandbox as the target runtime (same container) to hit the same libs/ops. That increases coverage but ties up capacity. alternative: ephemeral runner with runtime image pulled.

maria: proposal: default run in ephemeral runner using the customer's runtime image (fast pull cache). policy: tokenization mismatch or runtime exception -> onboarding fail; perf regress or tail-latency outlier -> advisory + ticket to infra.

aj: we should also wire in a quick telemetry export: shim result should include exact tokenizer hash, runtime binary hash, docker image tag, and a deterministic diff artifact. that helps debugging.

maria: agreed. example log output idea: 
```
[shim] model: open-model-x v1.2.0
[shim] tokenizer_hash: sha256:abc123
[shim] tokenize_diff: 1 mismatch at token 7 -> expected 'Ġthe' got 'the'
[shim] kv_probe: pass
[shim] perf_tps: 4800 (threshold 5000) -> advisory
```

cheng: small nit — diffs should be normalized to unicode and whitespace. many false positives come from unicode normalization.

leo: +1 normalization. also add a small retry/backoff for docker pulls (network flakes). ops-bot can annotate failures that look like infra flakiness.

ops-bot: note: last 7 days we had 4 docker pull flakes in us-west-2; suggest using regional mirror.

maria: actionables: (1) i will prototype the shim adapter interface and a runner in the bench repo (2) cheng will draft tokenizer artifact versioning rules (3) leo will sketch adapter examples for triton and llm-runtime images (4) aj will design failure taxonomy (block vs advisory). i'll open a short RFC-ish PR with the contract and example logs.

aj: sgtm. one more ask — include a minimal golden-input set per model (from owner) + a default fallback set. owners should be able to opt-out but must accept advisory risk.

maria: yep. opt-out requires explicit accept of advisory checklist. thanks all. i'll post the PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

leo: thanks — excited to see the prototype.

ops-bot: reminder: creating a shim runner will add ~2k jobs/month to bench CI cost estimate. tagged for finance review.
